title: Geometry - Lesson 4 Assessment: Explaining Perpendicular Constructions
description: Show mastery by selecting accurate construction steps, checking precision, and explaining why perpendicular constructions form right angles.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why line r is perpendicular to line $\ell$?
options: Line r is longer than line $\ell$.
Line r touches line $\ell$ at exactly one point and forms a $90^\circ$ angle.
Line r is drawn darker than line $\ell$.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines intersect to form right angles.

questions.question: A task says: Construct a perpendicular to line m through point A, where A is on line m. Which result is correct?
options: A line that forms $90^\circ$ with m but misses point A
A line through A that forms $90^\circ$ with m
A line through A that forms $80^\circ$ with m
questions.explanation: The construction must satisfy both conditions: through A and perpendicular to m.

questions.question: If one angle formed by two intersecting lines is $90^\circ$, the lines are perpendicular.
questions.explanation: One right angle is enough to identify perpendicular lines.

questions.question: The point where a perpendicular segment from an off-line point meets the given line is called the ______ of the perpendicular.
questions.explanation: The foot of the perpendicular is the meeting point on the original line.

questions.question: When using a set square to draw a perpendicular from point Q to line $\ell$, what should you do?
options: Keep one side along $\ell$ and slide it until another side passes through Q.
Put the calculator on Q and draw around it.
Choose any point on $\ell$ and connect it to Q.
Draw a line parallel to $\ell$ through Q.
questions.explanation: A set square has a right angle, so sliding it while one side stays on the line helps create a perpendicular through Q.

questions.question: A constructed angle measures $91^\circ$ when checked with a protractor. What should the student do?
options: Accept it because 91 is close to 90.
Erase or adjust the construction because perpendicular means exactly $90^\circ$.
questions.explanation: Construction precision matters. A perpendicular construction should form a right angle.

questions.question: If $\overleftrightarrow{AB} \perp \overleftrightarrow{CD}$, then the angle where the lines meet measures ______ degrees.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular symbol tells us the lines form right angles.

questions.question: Explain why a line constructed through point P is not correct if it forms $90^\circ$ with line $\ell$ but does not pass through P.
questions.correctAnswer: It is not correct because the task requires the perpendicular line to pass through P. Forming 90 degrees is necessary, but the line must also meet the required point condition.
questions.explanation: Construction tasks often have both an angle condition and a point condition.

questions.question: Write a complete explanation for this result: line t was drawn through point B on line n using a protractor mark at $90^\circ$.
questions.correctAnswer: Line t passes through B and forms a 90-degree angle with line n. Since lines that meet at 90 degrees are perpendicular, t is perpendicular to n.
questions.explanation: A complete explanation names the point condition, the right-angle evidence, and the perpendicular conclusion.

questions.question: A student says, "These lines are not perpendicular because neither line is vertical." Correct the student's reasoning.
questions.correctAnswer: Lines do not have to be vertical to be perpendicular. They are perpendicular if they intersect to form a 90-degree angle, even when both lines are slanted.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular is determined by the angle between the lines, not their orientation on the page.
